Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

bad adjective

of food: gone off

also gone off, go bad, go off, spoiled, spoilt, rotten

classical

Cato Agr. 3.2: nē corrumpātur
Cic. N.D. 2.20, of standing water (Lewis & Short)

corruptus, corrupta, corruptum

adjective (participle of corrumpō)

spoiled, gone bad

“To go bad” is the passive, corrumpī: corrumpitur, it is going off. Milk or wine that turns sour acēscit (see turn sour).

Other words

  • pūtidus, pūtida, pūtidum — rotten, stinking

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 19, of meat (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Trin. 2.4.125, of wine (Lewis & Short)

    Of meat, fish or fruit that smells.

Examples

  • cernis ut ignāvum corrumpant ōtia corpus, ut capiant vitium, nī moveantur, aquae

    you see how idleness spoils a lazy body, and how water goes bad if it doesn’t moveOv. Pont. 1.5.5–6

  • olea ubi lēcta siet, oleum fīat continuō, nē corrumpātur

    once the olives have been picked, the oil should be made at once, so that they don’t go badCato Agr. 3.2

See also bad, turn sour, sour.

SourcesLewis & Short: corrumpo · Lewis & Short: putidus
